title: Composing the Final Bill for an Event That Has Been Held
content:
The final bill for a Private Event & Banquet Services event that has been held is the food and beverage actually consumed, as the delivered entry standing in the event ledger records it.

## The parts

1. **Food and beverage.** The value actually consumed at the event, as the delivered entry standing in the event ledger records it.
2. **Room rental.** The room rental printed against the package is added to it in full.
3. **Service charge.** The service charge printed against the package is worked on the food and beverage the bill is priced on — that being the value actually consumed as the delivered entry records it — and added. No service charge is worked on the room rental, on the audio-visual package or on the bar minimum.

The bill is the food and beverage the bill is priced on, the room rental and that service charge added together and rounded to two decimal places at the end only, the parts themselves being left unrounded.

## Worked figure on hypothetical records

An event sits on the Conference Day Delegate Package, whose room rental is 450 and whose service charge is 20 per cent. The delivered entry records 7400 actually consumed.

| Part | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Food and beverage the bill is priced on | 7400 |
| Room rental printed against the package | 450 |
| Service charge, being 20 per cent of 7400 | 1480 |
| Bill, rounded at the end only | 9330.00 |

Where a part carries a fraction of a cent — a service charge of 1480.014 on a consumed value of 7400.07 — it is carried into the total as it stands, and the two decimal places are taken once, on the sum.

## Point of judgement

The service charge is worked on the food and beverage the bill is priced on and never on the room rental added at the second step, so the room rental enlarges the bill by its own figure alone.
